title: The new route list
scenario: The ferry company hands you a new list of route pairs. Build the map: each stop to the stops its routes lead to.

intro.job: The ferry company hands you a new list of route pairs. Build the map: each stop to the stops its routes lead to.

idea.rule: The dict IS the map — each stop's list grows as you read the pairs.
idea.detail: Same job as Build the map, new routes. Each pair is a one-way route [from, to]. Each stop gets a list of the stops its routes lead to — and a stop with two routes out needs both in its list. So make each stop's list once, and append every new route to it. A stop that only appears as a target still belongs on the map, with an empty list.

model_restatement: Build the adjacency dict from a list of one-way routes: each stop maps to the list of stops its routes lead to.

clarify.question: What if a stop has two routes out?
clarify.answer: Its list holds both, in the order the pairs give them — marina goes to ['channel', 'beacon'].

clarify.question: What about a dead end, a stop that goes nowhere?
clarify.answer: It still gets a key, with an empty list — like the shoal: [].

clarify.question: What about a stop that only appears as a target?
clarify.answer: It still belongs on the map — give it an empty list the first time you see it.

clarify.question: Which way does a pair point — what's the order?
clarify.answer: Each pair is [from, to]: a one-way route from the first stop to the second.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Start with an empty map. For each pair, set the first stop's routes to the second stop, and make sure the second stop is on the map too.

checkpoints.prompt: The first pass of the loop reads a pair. Which stop is a?

With the fix — on the third pass, after the append, what is graph?

why_line: The draft assigns graph[a] = [b] for every pair — so marina's second route replaces its first, and the map says marina goes only to beacon.

explain.rule: Assigning a fresh list is wiping a whiteboard: each new route for a stop erases the ones written before it.
explain.bridge: Marina's first pair writes ['channel']. What happens to that list when marina's second pair comes along?

fix.rule: Make each stop's list once, then append to it: graph[a].append(b) keeps every route.

walk.gloss: Only a stop seen for the first time gets a new list.
Add the route to the list that's already there.
A stop that's only a target...

alternatives.note: setdefault makes the list only if the stop isn't there yet, and hands back the list either way — one line per stop.

hints: Follow marina: what is graph['marina'] after its first pair, and after its second?
graph[a] = [b] makes a brand-new list every time — the old one is thrown away.
Make the list once (if a not in graph: graph[a] = []), then graph[a].append(b).
